title: Marked lifting test for cocartesian fibrations
statement: Use marked coanodyne maps and marked simplicial sets from [def-coef-infinity-marked-coanodyne], and the horn definition of cocartesian edges and fibrations from [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $E,B$ be small quasicategories, let $p:E\to B$ be a simplicial map, and let $T\subseteq E_1$ contain the degenerate edges. Then $(E,T)\to B^\sharp$ has the right lifting property against every marked coanodyne map if and only if $p$ is a cocartesian fibration and $T$ is exactly the set of $p$-cocartesian edges. The right lifting property is for commutative squares of marked maps and requires a marked diagonal over the specified base map.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.1.6 and Remark 3.1.1.10, opposite-category dual, with the target marked sharply. Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical assertion.

proof.text: Let $J$ be the four generating families (i)-(iv) of [def-coef-infinity-marked-coanodyne]. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-marked-coanodyne-rlp-saturation] to $q:(E,T)\to B^\sharp$: lifting against every marked coanodyne map is equivalent to lifting against every member of $J$. All squares and diagonals here are marked maps over the specified simplicial base map.

source.place: Definition 3.1.1.1, opposite-category dual; generator reduction for Proposition 3.1.1.6

proof.text: Suppose $q$ lifts the four generating families. By [def-coef-infinity-marked-coanodyne], family (i) is exactly the inner-horn test for $p$ in [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]: minimal markings require only preservation of degenerate edges. For family (ii) and $n\geq2$, the edge $\{0,1\}$ already belongs to $\Lambda_0^n$. Thus every initial-horn problem whose initial edge is in $T$ is a marked square of type (ii), and its diagonal is the defining cocartesian filler. Hence every edge of $T$ is $p$-cocartesian. For $n=1$, $\Lambda_0^1=\{0\}$, so (ii) gives an edge in $T$ over every base edge with any prescribed source. These are precisely the inner-fibration and existence conditions defining a cocartesian fibration.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.1.6, forward direction, printed pp. 149-150, opposite-category dual: comparison in a fibre, its Kan core, and generators (iv) then (iii)

proof.text: Fix a $p$-cocartesian edge $e:x\to y$ over $\alpha:p(x)\to b$. The preceding step supplies $t:x\to z$ in $T$ over the same $\alpha$; it also shows that $t$ is $p$-cocartesian. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality] to these two initial objects of $L(x,\alpha)$. Its comparison morphism from $t$ to $e$ is represented by a triangle $\sigma$ with ordered edges $[0,1]=t$, $[1,2]=u:z\to y$, $[0,2]=e$, lying over $s_1\alpha$. The same cited statement says that $u$ is an equivalence in the fibre $E_b$. This supplies the specified triangle and vertical equivalence used next.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.1.6, forward direction, printed pp. 149-150, opposite-category dual: comparison in a fibre, its Kan core, and generators (iv) then (iii)

proof.text: The fibre $F=E_b$ is a small quasicategory: given an inner horn in $F$, use the inner-fibration condition of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] to fill it in $E$ over the constant base simplex at $b$; the filler lies in $F$. The map $F\to\Delta^0$ is an isofibration as defined in [lem-coef-infinity-core-kan-fibration]: it lifts inner horns by this argument and lifts the sole base equivalence at each vertex by its degenerate edge. That node makes $F^\simeq\to(\Delta^0)^\simeq=\Delta^0$ a Kan fibration. Consequently $K=F^\simeq$ is a small Kan complex. Its edges include the equivalence $u$ from the preceding step by the stated definition of the core.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.1.6, forward direction, printed pp. 149-150, opposite-category dual: comparison in a fibre, its Kan core, and generators (iv) then (iii)

proof.text: Apply family (iv) of [def-coef-infinity-marked-coanodyne] to $K^\flat\to(E,T)$ given by inclusion and $K^\sharp\to B^\sharp$ constant at $b$. The top map is marked because $T$ contains degeneracies. The generator is the identity on underlying simplicial sets, so any diagonal is the same inclusion and marks every edge of $K$, including $u$. The triangle $\sigma$ now has its consecutive edges $t,u$ in $T$. Applying family (iii) over $s_1\alpha$ again fixes the underlying simplex and marks its diagonal edge $e$. Since $e$ was arbitrary, every $p$-cocartesian edge lies in $T$. Together with Step 2 this proves the forward implication, including equality of the marking.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.1.6, forward direction, printed pp. 149-150, opposite-category dual: comparison in a fibre, its Kan core, and generators (iv) then (iii)

proof.text: Conversely suppose that $p$ is a cocartesian fibration and $T$ is exactly its cocartesian edges. Family (i) in [def-coef-infinity-marked-coanodyne] lifts by the inner-fibration condition of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and every filler preserves the minimal marking. For (ii) with $n=1$, the horn $\Lambda_0^1=\{0\}$ specifies the source, and the cocartesian-fibration condition supplies a lift of the specified base edge from that source; the lift lies in $T$. For (ii) with $n\geq2$, the first edge $\{0,1\}$ is already in the horn and its image is marked, hence $p$-cocartesian. The defining initial-horn condition gives a filler over the given base simplex. It preserves the target marking because that marking adds only degeneracies and this already prescribed first edge. These are all cases of (i) and (ii).

source.place: Proposition 3.1.1.6, converse for generator families (1) and (2), opposite-category dual

proof.text: For a square against (iii), let $\sigma:\Delta^2\to E$ be its given underlying simplex. Its consecutive edges are in $T$, so both are $p$-cocartesian. The composition clause of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality] makes the diagonal edge $p$-cocartesian and hence marked. Thus the same $\sigma$ is the marked diagonal against (iii), still over the given base simplex.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.1.6, converse for generator (3), and Proposition 2.4.1.7, opposite-category duals

proof.text: For a square against (iv), let $f:K\to E$ be the given underlying map, where $K$ is Kan. By [lem-coef-infinity-core-kan-fibration], every edge of $K$ is an equivalence. Applying $f$ to each inverse edge and its two witnessing $2$-simplices shows that each image edge is an equivalence in $E$. The initial-horn assertion of [lem-cbc-inner-fibration-equivalence-outer-horn-lift] applies to $p$ (an inner fibration between the given small quasicategories): every prescribed $\Lambda_0^n$ problem, $n\geq2$, whose initial edge is such an equivalence has a filler over its specified base simplex. By the definition in [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], each image edge is therefore $p$-cocartesian. Equality of the marking puts all these edges in $T$, so $f$ itself is the required marked map $K^\sharp\to(E,T)$ over the original base map. We have proved lifting for all four families, and Step 1 gives lifting against every marked coanodyne map.

Statement: it is the opposite dual of HTT Prop 3.1.1.6 over B^sharp for small quasicategories. Generators (i)-(iv) of def-coef-infinity-marked-coanodyne are the duals of HTT 3.1.1.1 (1)-(4). Step 2 is elementary and correct: (ii) with n>=2 is exactly the cocartesian horn filler condition for edges in T, and (ii) with n=1 gives lifts from a prescribed source. Step 3: the composition-initiality statement gives the comparison triangle sigma=(t,u,e) over s_1 alpha, with u an equivalence in E_b. A 1-simplex of E_{x/} lying over the constant vertex gives exactly this. Step 4: E_b is a quasicategory because inner horns fill over the degenerate base simplex. E_b->Delta^0 meets the core node's isofibration definition, so the core is Kan and contains u. Step 5: the (iv) square has the same underlying map, so u is in T; the (iii) square on sigma then puts e in T, so T is exactly the cocartesian edges. Steps 6-8 are the converse: Step 6 handles (i) and (ii), Step 7 uses the composition clause, and Step 8 uses Kan edges being equivalences, which simplicial maps preserve, plus the outer-horn lemma, whose hypotheses all hold. Edge cases checked: n=1 and n=2, empty E, empty K, the identity with sharp marking, and the walking isomorphism over a point (it fails (iv) as it should).
